title: "2. Genotype quality control"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true

editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: inline
---

A PRS adds up thousands of small effects, so a few bad samples or SNPs can shift it. Here we check the genotypes and remove what fails. **plink2** does the heavy lifting; we run it from R with `run_tool()`, read its output back into R and decide the thresholds by looking at plots.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
source("config.R")
source("R/functions.R")
groups <- read_tsv(file.path(RESULTS, "cohort_groups.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## 1. Missing genotypes

```{r}
run_tool(PLINK2, c("--bfile", GENO, "--missing", "--out", file.path(QC_DIR, "raw")), "qc_missing")
smiss <- read_plink(file.path(QC_DIR, "raw.smiss"))   # per sample
vmiss <- read_plink(file.path(QC_DIR, "raw.vmiss"))   # per SNP
```

Choose your thresholds here, then look at the plots and change them if needed.

```{r}
MIND <- 0.05   # remove samples missing more than 5% of genotypes
GENO_MAX <- 0.02   # remove SNPs missing in more than 2% of samples
```

```{r, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.5}
p1 <- ggplot(smiss, aes(F_MISS)) + geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = MIND, colour = "#B2182B", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Per sample", x = "Proportion missing", y = "Samples") + theme_workshop()
p2 <- ggplot(vmiss, aes(F_MISS)) + geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = GENO_MAX, colour = "#B2182B", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Per SNP", x = "Proportion missing", y = "SNPs") + theme_workshop()
p1 + p2
smiss %>% filter(F_MISS > MIND)
cat(sum(vmiss$F_MISS > GENO_MAX), "SNPs above the threshold\n")
```

## 2. Allele frequency and Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium

Very rare SNPs add noise to a PRS. A strong departure from Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium usually means a genotyping error.

```{r}
run_tool(PLINK2, c("--bfile", GENO, "--freq", "--hardy", "--out", file.path(QC_DIR, "raw")), "qc_freq_hwe")
freq  <- read_plink(file.path(QC_DIR, "raw.afreq"))
hardy <- read_plink(file.path(QC_DIR, "raw.hardy"))

MAF_MIN <- 0.01
HWE_P   <- 1e-6
```

```{r, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.5}
freq <- freq %>% mutate(MAF = pmin(ALT_FREQS, 1 - ALT_FREQS))
p1 <- ggplot(freq, aes(MAF)) + geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = MAF_MIN, colour = "#B2182B", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Minor allele frequency", x = "MAF", y = "SNPs") + theme_workshop()
p2 <- ggplot(hardy, aes(-log10(P))) + geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = -log10(HWE_P), colour = "#B2182B", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Hardy-Weinberg test", x = "-log10(P)", y = "SNPs") + theme_workshop()
p1 + p2
cat(sum(freq$MAF < MAF_MIN), "SNPs below the MAF threshold;", sum(hardy$P < HWE_P), "SNPs fail HWE\n")
```

**Question.** Look at the SNPs failing HWE. Do they have too many or too few heterozygotes? (Compare `O(HET_A1)` with `E(HET_A1)`.)

```{r}
hardy %>% filter(P < HWE_P) %>% select(ID, `O(HET_A1)`, `E(HET_A1)`, P) %>% head()
```

## 3. Apply the sample and SNP filters

```{r}
step1 <- file.path(QC_DIR, "step1")
run_tool(PLINK2, c("--bfile", GENO, "--mind", MIND, "--geno", GENO_MAX, "--maf", MAF_MIN, "--hwe", HWE_P,
                   "--make-bed", "--out", step1), "qc_step1")
```

## 4. Independent SNPs for the next checks

Heterozygosity, relatedness and principal components should use SNPs that are not in linkage disequilibrium (LD) with each other. We "prune" them: in windows of 200 SNPs, drop one of any pair with r2 > 0.1.

```{r}
run_tool(PLINK2, c("--bfile", step1, "--indep-pairwise", 200, 50, 0.1, "--out", file.path(QC_DIR, "prune")), "qc_prune")
PRUNED <- file.path(QC_DIR, "prune.prune.in")
cat(length(readLines(PRUNED)), "independent SNPs kept\n")
```

## 5. Heterozygosity

Too many heterozygous calls suggests a contaminated sample (DNA from two people); too few suggests inbreeding or a poor sample. The F coefficient measures this; the usual rule removes samples more than 3 SD from the mean.

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.5}
run_tool(PLINK2, c("--bfile", step1, "--extract", PRUNED, "--het", "--out", file.path(QC_DIR, "het")), "qc_het")
het <- read_plink(file.path(QC_DIR, "het.het"))
het_lim <- mean(het$F) + c(-3, 3) * sd(het$F)
ggplot(het, aes(F)) + geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = het_lim, colour = "#B2182B", linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Heterozygosity (F)", y = "Samples") + theme_workshop()
het_out <- het %>% filter(F < het_lim[1] | F > het_lim[2])
het_out
```

## 6. Relatedness and duplicates

Comparing groups assumes the people are unrelated. KING estimates kinship for each pair: about 0.5 means the same person (duplicate or identical twin), about 0.25 first-degree relatives, about 0.125 second-degree. We list pairs above 0.0884 (second-degree or closer).

We leave out the heterozygosity outliers first: a contaminated sample carries DNA from two people, so it looks "related" to other contaminated samples. (Try it: delete the `--remove` part and run the chunk again.)

```{r}
write_tsv(het_out %>% select(FID, IID), file.path(QC_DIR, "het_outliers.txt"), col_names = FALSE)
run_tool(PLINK2, c("--bfile", step1, "--extract", PRUNED, "--remove", file.path(QC_DIR, "het_outliers.txt"),
                   "--make-king-table", "--king-table-filter", 0.0884,
                   "--out", file.path(QC_DIR, "king")), "qc_king")
king <- read_plink(file.path(QC_DIR, "king.kin0")) %>%
  mutate(relationship = case_when(KINSHIP > 0.354 ~ "duplicate / identical twin",
                                  KINSHIP > 0.177 ~ "first degree",
                                  TRUE            ~ "second degree"))
king %>% select(IID1, IID2, KINSHIP, relationship)
```

From each pair we remove one person. Our rule, decided before looking at any PRS: **keep the person with clinical data; if both have it, keep the one with fewer missing genotypes.** (Some studies instead keep the person with a genetic finding, to keep the rarer group as large as possible.)

```{r}
miss_lookup <- setNames(smiss$F_MISS, smiss$IID)
has_clin <- function(id) id %in% groups$IID
related_out <- king %>%
  mutate(remove = case_when(has_clin(IID1) & !has_clin(IID2) ~ IID2,
                            has_clin(IID2) & !has_clin(IID1) ~ IID1,
                            miss_lookup[IID1] >= miss_lookup[IID2] ~ IID1,
                            TRUE ~ IID2)) %>%
  pull(remove) %>% unique()
related_out
```

**Your turn.** The duplicate pair: is one of them the sample without a clinical record that we noticed in notebook 1?

```{r}

# king %>% filter(relationship == "duplicate / identical twin") %>%
#   mutate(IID1_has_clinical = IID1 %in% groups$IID, IID2_has_clinical = IID2 %in% groups$IID)
```

## 7. Remove the failed samples and save the clean genotypes

```{r}
remove <- tibble(IID = unique(c(het_out$IID, related_out)))
write_tsv(remove %>% mutate(FID = IID, .before = 1), file.path(QC_DIR, "remove.txt"), col_names = FALSE)
QC_GENO <- file.path(QC_DIR, "cohort_qc")
run_tool(PLINK2, c("--bfile", step1, "--remove", file.path(QC_DIR, "remove.txt"), "--make-bed", "--out", QC_GENO),
         "qc_final")
```

```{r}
qc_summary <- tibble(
  step = c("Start", "High missingness", "Heterozygosity", "Related or duplicate", "Final"),
  samples = c(nrow(smiss), sum(smiss$F_MISS > MIND), nrow(het_out), length(related_out),
              nrow(read_table(paste0(QC_GENO, ".fam"), col_names = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE))))
qc_summary
cat("SNPs:", nrow(vmiss), "before,", length(readLines(paste0(QC_GENO, ".bim"))), "after QC\n")
```
